question: To combat global warming and air pollution, several Member States, regions, and cities have established low emission zones (LEZs). In many cases, vehicles must display a sticker certifying their compliance with local emission laws to enter these zones1. However, travellers often face the challenge of obtaining multiple stickers or only discovering too late that a national or local LEZ sticker is required.
Introducing a single, standardised sticker for all LEZs across the EU could greatly simplify travel for EU citizens and reduce the administrative burden. 1.

Does the Commission acknowledge that introducing a single, standardised LEZ sticker, valid across all the Member States, could significantly simplify travel within the EU, reduce the administrative burden for both EU citizens and the authorities, and enhance compliance with environmental regulations?

What measures could the Commission envisage or undertake to develop a unified LEZ verification mechanism aimed at harmonising LEZ access requirements across the EU, improving the overall quality of life for EU citizens and upholding environmental standards?
Is the Commission prepared to initiate a legislative or policy-driven process to create and implement a standardised EU-wide LEZ sticker, ensuring consistency and ease of use for all EU citizens?

‘Milieuvignet: zo voorkom je boete van honderden euro’s tijdens jouw autovakantie’, Algemeen Dagblad website, 25 July 2024, https://www.ad.nl/auto/milieuvignet-zo-voorkom-je-boete-van-honderden-eurostijdens-jouw-autovakantie~a187f9a6/.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (8.12.2025) The design and implementation of urban vehicle access regulations (UVARs) like low emission zones (LEZs) is the responsibility of Member States and their respective authorities in line with the EU subsidiarity principle.

As compliance schemes cater for the specific needs of the local population and reflect the administrative capacity of the competent authorities that differ in budget, staffing or technical expertise, it is unclear whether a single scheme would indeed enhance UVAR compliance.

The Commission introduced measures to foster LEZ information provision via Regulations 2022/6701 that provides EU-wide real-time traffic information (including LEZ data) and 2018/17242 that includes the publication of traffic rules, including UVARs, and of online procedures for obtaining LEZ stickers. The Commission conducted a study3 to identify solutions for demonstrating compliance with access rules.

The goal was to support the operation of more efficient, easy-to-use, and nondiscriminatory EU-wide UVARs. Study recommendations, which may serve in future policy initiatives, are currently under assessment (including an EU Digital Wallet based solution).
1 Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/670 of 2 February 2022 supplementing Directive 2010/40/EU of

the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to the provision of EU-wide real-time traffic information services, OJ L 122, 25.4.2022, pp. 1–16, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg_del/2022/670/oj.

2 Regulation (EU) 2018/1724 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 2 October 2018 establishing a single digital gateway to provide access to information, to procedures and to assistance and problem-solving services and amending Regulation (EU) No 1024/2012, OJ L 295, 21.11.2018, pp. 1–38, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2018/1724/oj.

3 Directorate-General for Mobility and Transport, AustriaTech, MAPtm, Panteia and TRT, Mapping study on digital and technical solutions to enable more effective and user-friendly UVARs – Final report, Publications Office of the European Union, 2025, https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2832/7516051.
